title: Allow a one time change to charging thresholds
line: When a charge limit is set, the battery applet has a Charge Fully Once button, and the limit comes back when the laptop is unplugged.
explanation: With a battery charge limit set (for example 40-80%), the only way to charge to 100% before a trip was to change the limit in System Settings and remember to change it back afterwards; the battery applet only said the battery charges up to about 80%. Powerdevil had no notion of a temporary change. Now the applet shows a Charge Fully Once button next to that hint. It asks powerdevil's root helper (with the same admin authentication as changing the limit in System Settings) to save the current limits in /var/lib/powerdevil and lift them to 0-100%; when the power cord is unplugged, also across a reboot, powerdevil puts the saved limits back through a new helper action that needs no password because it can only restore what an admin already set. The hint then reads 'Battery will charge fully until the power cord is unplugged.' with a Cancel button, and setting new limits in System Settings drops the saved ones.

commits.message:
applets/batterymonitor: add a button to charge the battery fully once

Charging past the charge limit for a trip meant raising it in System
Settings and remembering to lower it again. The battery applet now
offers to charge fully once, and powerdevil restores it when unplugged.

BUG: 445965

media.caption: Plugged in with a 40-80% charge limit: the applet only says the battery charges up to about 80%
Charge Fully Once lifts the limit (the hint changes and offers Cancel); unplugging restores 40-80% and plugging back in shows the 80% limit again
